description.value: A controlled fMRI study investigated the neural substrate of smoking-related attentional bias and its association with subjective craving in smokers compared with nonsmoking controls.

spans.text: The objective of the current study was to investigate the neural substrate of attentional bias and associated subjective craving in smokers.

description.value: A controlled, age- and gender-matched, single-session study comparing smokers and nonsmoking controls.

spans.text: A group of smokers ( n = 20) and a group of age- and gender-matched nonsmoking controls ( n = 22) were recruited from the general population and participated in a single session of fMRI scanning while attentional processes were manipulated.

value: Overall cognitive effort during line counting was associated with robust brain activation in bilateral occipital, parietal, and prefrontal brain regions, as well as in motor areas, the ACC, and several subcortical regions. Smokers showed less brain activation associated with overall cognitive effort than controls in the rvACC, left caudate nucleus, left intraparietal lobe, left lingual gyrus, and left parahippocampal gyrus.

value: Both groups showed more activation in visual, parietal, and motor areas during cue exposure-corrected attention. Smokers showed more brain activation related to cue exposure-corrected attention for smoking cues than controls in the rostral zone of the dACC, confirming that attentional bias-related brain activation in this region does not arise from mere cue exposure effects.

name.value: Self-reported craving during the attentional bias paradigm

definition.value: Self-reported craving in smokers during the attentional bias paradigm was significantly associated with activation in the right putamen and the left insula.

label.value: self-reported craving during the attentional bias paradigm

value: Self-reported craving during the attentional bias paradigm was significantly associated with activation in the right putamen and the left insula. This suggests that these regions are involved in the reciprocal relation between attentional bias and craving.
